prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: دورات تدريبية معتمدة (language ar, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 5 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 13px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "اسم الدورة" · longest unbreakable word 58px · one-line width 218px
  col 2: header "المدة" · longest unbreakable word 44px · one-line width 147px
  col 3: header "المدرب" · longest unbreakable word 48px · one-line width 92px
  col 4: header "الوصف" · longest unbreakable word 63px · one-line width 1235px
  col 5: header "الرسوم" · longest unbreakable word 37px · one-line width 62px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 599px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 598px.
Fixed: content, font, 13px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"A catalogue of accredited training courses: readers browse course names, compare duration and fee, and use the description for detail before choosing.","reading":"Right-to-left and row-first: the rightmost course name is the entry point, then duration and trainer, then the long description, with the fee at the far left as a quick check. Comparison is mainly identity plus duration/fee; description is read only after a row interests the reader.","groups":["cols 1 and 5: identity and price are the primary decision anchors and benefit from staying intact","cols 2 and 3: short logistics metadata that play the same compact supporting role","col 4: long prose description, functionally separate from the scannable metadata"],"keep_intact":["col 1 course names: no mid-word breaks; longest unbreakable word is 58px","col 5 fee values: keep as one line/one token; 62px content width","col 2 numerals and units: keep numbers with their units where possible","col 3 trainer names: keep honorific/title with the name where possible"],"may_wrap":["col 4 description: prose, expected to wrap over many lines","col 1 long course names: wrap at spaces between words","col 2 duration phrases: wrap between number and unit or before parenthetical hours","col 3 trainer names: wrap between title and name parts"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r0A: widths [130, 80, 75, 230, 83] · table 599×837px · row heights [33, 154, 134, 114, 134, 134, 134] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 7 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0B: widths [239, 75, 70, 131, 83] · table 599×1502px · row heights [33, 275, 235, 214, 235, 255, 255] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 13 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0C: widths [150, 115, 100, 150, 83] · table 599×1240px · row heights [33, 235, 194, 194, 174, 194, 214] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 11 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}

log.raw: {"critique":[{"design":"r0A","good":"Best of the three: the description takes the largest share (230px), so the table stays comparatively short (837px) and rows read as units. The column order of widths (name > description > duration > trainer ≈ fee) roughly matches the reading order.","problems":"The identity column is choppy: 130px leaves 109px of text, so course names break into 2–3 lines and the eye cannot sweep the names. The description still reaches 7 lines, so it alone drives the 134–154px row heights.","cause":"The budget is close but not resolved: 230px is still below the width where the 1235px description text drops a line, while the three short columns are squeezed under 90px.
